plan: Given my value of $25, I aim to maximize profit while considering potential bids by Betty and Charles. Assuming rational behavior, they might bid near their values. To win, I should bid slightly above the midpoint of the value range. A bid of $20 balances winning chances and potential profit. If they bid higher, I lose nothing; if lower, I win with profit ($25 value - $20 bid = $5 profit). This strategy optimizes my outcome given the uncertainty of their bids.

I aim to maximize profit by balancing a competitive bid with the risk of overpaying. Given my value of $18, I should bid below this to ensure a positive profit if I win. Assuming others bid close to their values, I will bid slightly less than my value to increase chances of winning without risking a loss. A bid of $15.5 offers a good balance, as it allows a profit of $2.5 if I win, while being competitive enough against potential bids from Andy and Charles.

Given my value of $31, I should aim to bid slightly below this to maximize profit if I win. Assuming Andy and Betty bid based on their values, I expect an average bid around $24. To win, I should slightly outbid the average but stay under my value. I’ll bid $25. This balances winning chances and profit. If outbid, I lose nothing. If I win, my profit is $31 - $25 = $6.
